title: Responding in Defender for Endpoint

header.html: Investigate device timelines; perform actions on the device, including live response and collecting investigation packages; perform evidence and entity investigation; investigate and remediate incidents identified by automatic attack disruption
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

toc.title: The device page and the timeline

html:
1The device page and the timeline

Open a device from Assets > Devices, from an alert, or by global search.

Tab Shows
Overview Active alerts, logged on users (past 30 days), security assessments, device health
Incidents and alerts Alerts and incidents for the device
Timeline Events on the device, in time order
Security recommendations, Software inventory, Discovered vulnerabilities, Missing KBs Exposure data from vulnerability management
Timeline fact Detail
Default range The past 30 days; filters for day, week, 30 days or a custom range
Export Up to seven days of events
Flags Flag key events to build a clean breach timeline
Hunt for related events Opens advanced hunting
Exam tip

. The timeline shows what happened on a device; flag the events that tell the attack story.

2Response actions on a device

Action What it does
Manage tags Labels the device (also used in dynamic scopes)
Initiate live response session A remote command-line session
Collect investigation package Gathers forensic data into a zip
Run antivirus scan Quick or full; default CPU cap 50%
Restrict app execution Allows only Microsoft-signed apps, using a code integrity policy; undo with Remove app restrictions
Isolate device Full or selective isolation
Contain device Blocks communication with the device from all onboarded devices
Consult a threat expert Microsoft Threat Experts

Plan 1 includes the manual actions run antivirus scan, isolate device, stop and quarantine a file, add an indicator; the others need Plan 2.

Isolation Detail
Full Disconnects the device from the network; Defender service connectivity stays
Selective Windows 10 1709 or later; can keep Outlook and Teams with isolation exclusions
Role Active remediation actions
Offline device Isolation is retried for up to three days
VPN A full tunnel blocks the Defender cloud; use split tunneling

Contain device: Microsoft recommends up to 100 devices at a time; it takes up to 5 minutes to propagate; undo with Release from containment.

Exam tip

. Isolate = this device is cut off. Contain = other devices stop talking to it (also used by attack disruption).

3Investigation package

Choose Collect investigation package, enter a comment, and the zip downloads (or download from Action center). Windows contents:

Group Items
System Autoruns, Installed programs, Processes, Services, Scheduled tasks, System information, Users and groups
Network Network connections (ActiveNetConnections, ARP, DNS cache, IP config, firewall logs), SMB sessions
Evidence Prefetch files, Security event log, Temp directories, WdSupportLogs, CollectionSummaryReport.xls

4Live response

Start: Device inventory > device > Initiate live response session. It must be turned on in Settings > Endpoints > Advanced features (and live response for servers). Basic and advanced commands are separate permissions in an RBAC custom role.

Basic commands Advanced commands
cd, cls, connect, connections, dir, drivers, fg, fileinfo, findfile, getfile, help, jobs, persistence, processes, registry, scheduledtasks, services, startupfolders, status, trace analyze, run, library, putfile, remediate, undo (plus collect, scan, isolate and release on macOS or Linux)
Command Use
getfile Download a file from the device
putfile Send a library file to the device
run Run a script from the library (do not use ; &
remediate Remove a file (delete), process (stop and delete), service, registry entry, scheduled task or startup item; undo reverts
Limit Value
Concurrent sessions 50 per organization; 5 per user; one per device
Inactivity timeout 30 minutes
Command timeout 10 minutes (30 minutes for getfile, findfile, run)
File sizes getfile 3 GB; library 250 MB; putfile 300 MB on Windows
Background jobs Add & to getfile or run; fg brings it back

Unsigned PowerShell scripts need the separate advanced feature Allow unsigned script execution in live response.

Exam tip

. Advanced live response is needed for run, putfile, library and remediate. getfile is basic.

5Evidence and entity investigation

Entity Key points
File page Observed in organization (devices up to six months, cloud apps 30 days); actions Stop and quarantine, Manage indicator, Download file, Collect file, Go hunt, Deep analysis
IP page Geo information, related alerts, activity on up to 100 devices, prevalence (default 30 days)
Domain or URL page Verdict, incidents and alerts, devices, emails and clicks (last 30 days)
User page Overview, Alerts, Observed in organization; the dashboard shows Users at risk

Stop and quarantine file: Windows 10 1703 or later; not for trusted non-Microsoft or Microsoft-signed files; up to 1,000 devices; times out after three days. Download file gives a password-protected zip and needs Download quarantined files. Deep analysis works on PE files only. Evidence verdicts are Malicious, Suspicious, No threats found.

6Incidents from automatic attack disruption

Incidents tagged Attack Disruption show the containment actions (Module 4). The analyst checks the timeline, keeps the containment while investigating, removes the threat, then releases the device or user from the Action center.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A device shows ransomware activity. The SOC wants to cut it off from the network but keep it reporting to Defender. Which action fits?

  • AIsolate device, with full isolation of the network traffic
  • BContain device, which blocks other devices from talking to it
  • CRestrict app execution, with a code integrity policy
  • DRun antivirus scan, with a full scan of all files
Show the answer

Answer: A. Full isolation disconnects the device from the network but keeps Defender service connectivity.

S2An analyst needs Autoruns, prefetch files, services and the security event log from a suspected device for forensic review. What should the analyst use?

  • ARun antivirus scan with a quick scan option
  • BLive response with the getfile command only
  • CRestrict app execution on the suspected device
  • DCollect investigation package, then download the zip file
Show the answer

Answer: D. The investigation package gathers those forensic items into a zip.

S3An analyst wants to run a prepared script from the live response library on a device. Which command and permission apply?

  • AThe getfile command with basic live response
  • BThe run command with advanced live response
  • CThe cd command with basic live response
  • DThe processes command with advanced live response
Show the answer

Answer: B. Run needs advanced live response; getfile and cd are basic commands.

S4A user already has five live response sessions open and tries a sixth. What happens?

  • AThe sixth session opens because the limit is 50 per user
  • BThe sixth session is blocked because the limit is 5 per user
  • CThe sixth session replaces the oldest session for the user
  • DThe sixth session opens after a 30 minute wait for that user
Show the answer

Answer: B. The limits are 50 concurrent sessions per organization and 5 per user.

S5An analyst chooses Stop and quarantine for a file signed by Microsoft. What is the result?

  • AThe action works but is limited to a single device
  • BThe action is not available for Microsoft-signed files
  • CThe action runs and then needs approval after three days
  • DThe action runs and also blocks the certificate tenant-wide
Show the answer

Answer: B. Stop and quarantine cannot be applied to trusted non-Microsoft or Microsoft-signed files.

S6What does the Restrict app execution action do?

  • ABlocks all network traffic from the device
  • BAllows only Microsoft-signed apps through a code integrity policy
  • CDeletes every unsigned file on the device
  • DDisables the user who is logged on the device
Show the answer

Answer: B. Restrict app execution applies a policy that allows only Microsoft-signed files.

7.2 Recall questions

R1How many live response sessions can one user have?

Show the answer

Five at the same time.

R2What is the getfile size limit?

Show the answer

3 GB.

R3How long is the live response inactivity timeout?

Show the answer

30 minutes.

R4Which role is needed to isolate a device?

Show the answer

Active remediation actions.

R5Which file type does deep analysis support?

Show the answer

PE files only.

R6How long can the timeline be exported?

Show the answer

Up to seven days.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Timeline default 30 days; flag events; export 7 days
Actions live response, investigation package, scan, restrict app, isolate, contain
Isolate vs contain isolate cuts the device off; contain blocks others from reaching it
Live response 50 sessions, 5 per user, 30 min idle; advanced for run, putfile, library, remediate
Limits getfile 3 GB, library 250 MB, putfile 300 MB
File actions stop and quarantine (1,000 devices, not Microsoft-signed), download, collect, deep analysis
